title: William Tutte
name: William Tutte
summary: British mathematician whose analysis of the German Lorenz cipher made high-level wartime cryptanalysis possible without seeing the machine.
whyThisMatters: Tutte’s reconstruction of the Lorenz cipher from intercepted traffic is a classic example of extracting a system’s structure from its outputs—the central intellectual move of cryptanalysis and security analysis.

sections.overview:
William Tutte was a British mathematician and wartime cryptanalyst at Bletchley Park. Working from intercepted ciphertext, he deduced the logical structure of the German Lorenz SZ40/42 cipher machine, known to British analysts as Tunny.

Lorenz and mechanised analysis

Tutte’s analysis enabled the later mechanisation of attacks on Lorenz traffic. That work formed part of the setting in which Colossus was developed and used for high-speed cryptanalytic processing.

In memoriam

Tutte died in 2002. He is remembered both for cryptanalysis and for major contributions to mathematics.

timeline.event: Deduces the structure of the Lorenz cipher machine from traffic.
Mechanised work against Tunny enters operation at Bletchley Park.
Emigrates to Canada and continues a mathematical career.
